findings.title: Distinguish a physically released CITY from a live retained CITY and a list draining after release
evidence: release marks a city record released and may leave it alive while its children remain. rejoin then accepts the same record because its list remains nonempty, without checking held.released. INSERT a fresh sector placement, LINK it to that released record before the last child leaves, and its old City state/box is transferred back into a live placement. The new tests only drain those children; they never try this continuation.

The newly admitted parked-record continuation also never checks the fresh destination entry is ENTITY_CITY. A non-CITY fresh entry with no first state can be joined to the retained City record before its later state report rejects the mismatch.

The Lua tracker clears city.lists[parent] immediately at RELEASE. A supported later CHILD_REMOVE for a still-listed child names the ended original sector key; request_join_problem then counts an ended-parent request fault, even though the real provider deliberately keeps that released list until its last child leaves.
findings.effect: The Host can resurrect or misbind physically ended CITY state, while the public diagnostic rejects a legitimate post-release drain. This contradicts the new phase16 lifetime contract and its no-new-valid-path-refusal requirement.
minimum_correction: Before mutating any entry, alias, record or object mapping, reject continuation of released CITY records and require the destination of a retained-CITY continuation to be an actual live CITY placement. Keep existing generic building-link semantics outside this new CITY path unchanged.

Track released-but-draining list lifetime separately from live placement/continuable retention in Lua. Permit its legitimate existing child removals, but no new continuation/insertion, and end its binding after the last child leaves.

Use the existing real provider/Lua collaborators for positive live relink and release-with-child drain controls, plus rejected post-release LINK and wrong-family parked LINK. Assert state/aliases/order remain unchanged on refusal. No new native bad-input experiment is required.

findings.title: Validate the retained-record relationship before modifying the C placement cache
evidence: place_remove calls place_forget_key(slot,0) before place_retain_record checks whether a named removal is a CITY and whether its existing list anchor matches. The new non-CITY/wrong-record negative controls stop by name but the C placement key/cache has already been changed.

When no list anchor is held, place_retain_record copies any syntactically valid name without joining it to the current CITY placement record. The new coherent no-anchor positive uses that placement’s own key; a different live/parked city key is not an authorized substitute.
findings.effect: An invalid retained-record acknowledgement can partially change C compatibility state or bind another City’s record before later rejection. Complete grammar validation in the shared exchange does not establish this caller-specific relationship.
minimum_correction: Validate CITY type and the returned retained-record relation against the already-held list anchor, or the current placement’s own record key when there is no prior anchor, before forgetting a key or writing a list name. Then apply accepted cache changes.

Extend the existing real C dialogue positive-first controls with wrong LIVE record, non-CITY and malformed retained acknowledgements. Snapshot and require unchanged placement keys, list anchors, aliases, naming flags and lookup state on rejection; preserve coherent relink/release order.

findings.title: The proposed provider replay does not exercise the changed Core lifecycle or a consuming collision path

This is another provider/roster contract test. It never invokes the changed actual Core placement-map lifecycle and does not identify an actual consuming collision stage.
findings.effect: A passing direct-provider replay could leave C retention, release ordering and the Core mirror/Host record join unexecuted. It cannot close REQUIRED_CITY_BOX_LIFECYCLE_RETENTION or provide the required native authority proof.
minimum_correction: Supply a bounded source-supported opt-in path through Host Lua -> native Core -> the actual shared CITY removal/relink/restore services on one real bound CITY, followed by an actual consuming collision path. If the current public fixture exposes no such operation, add the smallest existing-profile fixture capability and review it; do not replace the path with fabricated provider questions or a second solver.

Declare the current real CITY/child/record binding and actual empty/relinked/restored prerequisite before credit. An empty-city early skip that never reads its box is not evidence of box consumption. No actor/time/geometry search or UNREACHED-as-pass.

Declare BOOT versus post-launch row phase, exact fields, named refusal/acknowledgement and no-postfatal-access contract before launch. Preserve all existing healthy fields, including the four fixed_rule diagnostics; explicitly declare any actual phase16 lifecycle-counter delta. Require complete physical-terminal and ordinary-short equality without normalization.

reviewed_behavior.lifetimes: Placement end, parked retention, diagnostic state withdrawal and physical entity release are now separate concepts. Their implementation must preserve the release/draining distinctions in finding1 and the C acknowledgement boundary in finding2.
